title: Flat local base change through a prescribed smooth closed-fibre point
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $q:L\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and let $x$ be a closed point of its closed fibre [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. There are a Noetherian local ring $B$, a flat local ring homomorphism $\varphi:A\to B$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and a morphism $s:\operatorname{Spec}B\to L$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, such that $s$ maps the closed point of $B$ to the image of $x$. The only point of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ mapping to the closed point of $A$ is its closed point.

proof.text: Use lem-sbc-smooth-closed-point-finite-flat-lift to obtain the finite flat local base A′ and a separable point y of the base-changed smooth scheme above x. Apply the existing etale-slice declaration attached to lem-sbc-smooth-separable-point-etale-slice to the smooth pullback projection at y, giving Z, i and z with i(z)=y and Z -> Spec A′ etale.

Set B to the stalk of Z at z; Z is locally Noetherian by local finite type over the Noetherian A′. By lem-sbc-canonical-stalk-spectrum-flat its canonical spectrum map is flat. Compose with the etale slice and finite flat base map to get a flat map t:Spec B -> Spec A. Spec.map_surjective extracts a ring homomorphism beta. The canonical closed-point formula gives t(m_B)=m_A; local_hom_TFAE applied to this equality proves beta is local.

Mathlib Hom.quasiFiniteAt_iff proves the localization of the etale slice locally quasi-finite; composition with the finite base map gives locally quasi-finite t. To reflect the closed point, any w specializes to m_B in the local spectrum. If t(w)=m_A=t(m_B), put both points in that fibre. Mathlib isDiscrete_preimage_singleton makes this fibre discrete, and IsInducing.subtypeVal.specializes_iff transports their specialization to its subtype. In a discrete space specialization implies equality, giving w=m_B. Compose the canonical map with i and the pullback first projection to get s; pullback.condition proves its base equation and the canonical closed-point and lift equations prove s(m_B)=q.fiber_i(x).

theorem exists_smooth_closed_point_local_section
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    {L : Scheme.{u}} (q : L ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [Smooth q]
    (x : q.fiber (IsLocalRing.closedPoint A)) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set _)) :
    ∃ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : IsLocalRing B) (_ : IsNoetherianRing B),
      ∃ (φ : A →+* B), IsLocalHom φ ∧ φ.Flat ∧
        (∀ z, (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)) z = IsLocalRing.closedPoint A →
          z = IsLocalRing.closedPoint B) ∧
        ∃ (s : Spec (.of B) ⟶ L), s ≫ q = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ) ∧
          s (IsLocalRing.closedPoint B) = q.fiberι (IsLocalRing.closedPoint A) x
